closed-datum-the-open-datum-application-.text: Closed datum: the open-datum application with every update refused.

The release archive carries one application, open-datum, in which the controller of a name can update the name's payload. This ticket adds a second on-chain entry point to that same application, in which the payload is written once at registration and every update is refused on chain. It is the on-chain half of issue 650; the executable's --closed choice at create is the next ticket. Issue 651.

story.text: As the presenter of Demo 1, I need the release archive to carry a closed-datum application. It is the same open-datum code from the same release, except that a name's payload is written once at registration and every update is refused on chain. Registration and termination, with the deposit back, behave as in open-datum. When a person with the archive reads its blueprint, they find the closed-datum validator beside the open-datum one, with its own pinned identity, and open-datum's identity is exactly the one every earlier rehearsal ran.

Nothing is runnable by a person yet. The executable gains the choice in the next ticket of issue 650, and a real node refuses a crafted update in the ticket after it. This ticket proves the validator in the Aiken suite and pins it in the release.

what-is-established.text: Read on main at cfe78df1 and measured on 15 October 2026 in a scratch copy of the tree that was never pushed.

The open-datum validator is validator open_datum(registry) in applications/open-datum/onchain/validators/open_datum.ak. Its spend handler has two paths: an update, which keeps the key's token at the same address with the same control and lets the payload change, and a release, which is allowed only inside the registry's fold that terminates the key and burns its token.

Aiken refuses a validator module that imports another validator module, unless the importing module is a test module. A second file closed_datum.ak that calls the open-datum handlers fails the production build with aiken::check::illegal::import: "I discovered an attempt to import a validator module in a library: 'open_datum'". Its help text says to move shared code into a library module, or to import a validator only for testing.

A second validator block placed in the same module builds, and calls the first validator's handlers by name. Built that way, the blueprint holds open_datum.open_datum.{mint,spend,else} with hash cdc67586fd5391249e862338e88120ec5921d3fc9f4cd84b8cce7c33, equal to the committed identity rows, and open_datum.closed_datum.{mint,spend,else} with a hash of its own. Aiken compiles each validator from the code it reaches, so a sibling validator does not enter open-datum's program; the equal hash is the control for that statement.
A test module that imports a validator may not export pub definitions, so the existing fixtures of open_datum.tests.ak, all private, cannot be imported by a second test file.

requirements.text: closed-spend-refuses-every-update: the closed-datum spend handler refuses the Update redeemer, with the trace label closed-datum-update, for every payload the suite already quantifies over, in a context that open-datum accepts. No context, signer or output shape turns an update into an acceptance.

closed-refusal-is-the-closed-rule: every context that closed-datum refuses as an update is accepted by open-datum's spend in the same test file, so the refusal is the closed rule and not a broken fixture.

closed-release-follows-open-release: the closed-datum spend handler passes Release to open-datum's spend handler. A release inside the registry's terminating fold, with the controller paid, is accepted, and the same transaction is accepted by the registry's state validator. A release outside that fold is refused, as open-datum refuses it.

closed-booking-follows-open-booking: the closed-datum mint handler is open-datum's mint handler. Booking an insertion and booking a termination are accepted, and a booking that open-datum refuses is refused with the same verdict.
closed-else-refuses: the closed-datum handler for any other script purpose fails, as open-datum's does.

closed-refusal-test-can-fail: the application's Aiken check proves that the closed rows ran and can fail. Its log names a closed refusal test, and a planted copy of open_datum.ak whose closed spend accepts Update makes the suite fail, naming that test. The plant confirms it applied before the suite runs.

open-datum-identity-unmoved: the open-datum rows of applications/open-datum/onchain/script-identity.json are byte-identical to main, and the identity job passes. The edit to open_datum.ak is an append of the new validator after its last line: no line of the file changes and no import changes.
closed-identity-pinned-from-the-build: the manifest gains the three closed rows, generated from the real blueprint and never typed; the identity job compares both directions.
seventeen-validators-in-the-release: wherever the merged validator count is asserted, 14 becomes 17: the merged deployment blueprint in the application's flake and the release assembler.

base-hash-comparison-admits-only-what-is-declared: the split-blueprint comparison keeps every base hash byte-identical, admits exactly the three declared closed-datum validators, and refuses any other extra validator and any declared validator whose hash differs from the manifest. Each refusal is shown by a plant that runs on every invocation.
registry-untouched: no change to the registry contract, its script hashes, the registry library or the singular commands.
no-lean-statement: the write-once rule has no Lean statement, by operator ruling (see the ruling page). It is not in the conformance suite or the theorem register, and nothing here claims otherwise.

why-a-second-validator-inside-open_datum.text: Why a second validator inside open_datum.ak.
Three ways to make closed-datum "a flag over open-datum" were weighed.

The chosen shape keeps three things. Open-datum's compiled hash and identity rows do not move, so every open-datum test, record and hosted job passes untouched. The registry library is not changed, because it loads application code by blueprint title and applies the one registry parameter, so the title open_datum.closed_datum works through the same path. And the difference between the two applications is the one place the spend handler names Update.

stated-limits.text: The write-once rule has no Lean statement. Lean remains the authority for every rule the closed-datum application shares with open-datum, which it reaches by calling open-datum's handlers.

This ticket evaluates the closed-datum validator in the Aiken suite only. The permanent compiled-code boundary keeps its four open-datum application contexts; running the compiled closed-datum code over a ledger is the later negative-host ticket of issue 650.
The executable's --closed choice, the client's refusal of an update before it signs, the devnet journey from the release archive and the negative-host part are the later tickets of issue 650.
